stories.title: Pakistan brokers a US–Iran ceasefire; Islamabad talks end without a deal
stories.summary: Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire conditional on Iran fully reopening Hormuz. Days later, Vice President JD Vance led talks with Iranian officials in Islamabad, which ended without a broader deal. Trump extended the ceasefire indefinitely on Apr 21, with Pakistan, Qatar and others continuing to mediate.

causes.why: Pressure on Iran's oil hub preceded the ceasefire
Six weeks of war

analysis.text: Pakistan gained standing in Washington and the Gulf as the indispensable mediator while at war with Afghanistan, a role that later helped it into the Saudi defence pact.

stories.title: Israel's heaviest Lebanon strikes stall the Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: A day into the US–Iran ceasefire, Israel launched its largest strikes of the war on Hezbollah across Lebanon, including Beirut. Some ships had begun to transit Hormuz, but CRS reports that Iran halted traffic in response to the Israeli attacks in Lebanon.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Timeline of the Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2 March 2026 – present)

causes.why: Continuing Lebanon front
Lebanon was left out of the ceasefire in practice

stories.title: Orbán ousted after 16 years as Magyar's Tisza wins a landslide
stories.summary: Péter Magyar's pro-EU Tisza party won a two-thirds majority in Hungary's election, ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule. Magyar promised a democratic reset with an eye on frozen EU funds.

analysis.text: Moscow lost its most reliable veto inside the EU and NATO.

stories.title: US imposes a naval blockade on Iranian ports
stories.summary: After the Islamabad talks failed, the US blockaded all shipping to and from Iranian ports from Apr 13. The ceasefire largely held. A US effort in May to escort ships out of the strait ('Project Freedom') was paused after two days, reportedly because Saudi Arabia refused the use of its airspace.

causes.why: Talks failed

analysis.text: Both sides now claimed to control the strait, Washington by blockade and Tehran by force. CRS says that dispute is what wrecked the June deal.

stories.unplaced: Enforced at sea around Iran's ports; no single site.

stories.title: China moves to block the entrance to Scarborough Shoal
stories.summary: Satellite images showed China moving to block the entrance to Scarborough Shoal, which the Philippines also claims. Beijing later proposed a national nature reserve at the shoal, which the US said in August was an effort to claim the South China Sea.

stories.title: EU finalises a €90bn Ukraine loan after Hungary lifts its veto
stories.summary: The EU Council finalised a €90 billion loan to Ukraine for 2026–27, funded by EU borrowing and backed by the EU budget, along with a 20th sanctions package. Ukraine repays only once it receives Russian reparations. Hungary dropped its veto after oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline resumed.

causes.why: Change of government ended the Hungarian veto
Repayment is tied to Russian assets frozen since 2022

stories.unplaced: A Council decision; no single site.

stories.title: JNIM and Tuareg rebels sweep Mali; Kidal falls and the defence minister is killed
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and the Tuareg separatist FLA launched coordinated attacks across Mali, including near Bamako and in Gao, Sévaré and Mopti. The FLA took Kidal after Malian troops and Russia's Africa Corps withdrew. Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed.

causes.why: French exit left Russia as Mali's sole security partner
Russian forces in Mali since 2021

analysis.text: Russia's Africa Corps could not hold several fronts at once, which dented Moscow's pitch as a regime protector in the Sahel.

stories.title: JNIM declares a blockade of Bamako
stories.summary: Days after its offensive, JNIM announced a full blockade of Mali's capital, setting up checkpoints, attacking trucks and calling on Malians to rise up. It had first targeted fuel imports in September 2025.

causes.why: Follow-on to the offensive

stories.title: UAE quits OPEC, exposing a deep Saudi rift
stories.summary: The UAE announced it would leave OPEC and OPEC+ from May 1 after nearly 60 years, citing its expanded capacity. Reuters reported the move laid bare a widening rift with Saudi Arabia, though OPEC+ was expected to hold together with a smaller share of world output.

causes.why: Saudi–UAE split over Yemen
Saudi-led quota politics the UAE resented

analysis.text: With Hormuz shut, the exit costs Abu Dhabi little now; it is a bet on pumping freely after the war and a statement of independence from Riyadh.

stories.title: Senate confirms Kevin Warsh as Fed chair as inflation climbs
stories.summary: The Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair by 54–45, largely along party lines, as inflation picked up.

causes.why: War-driven energy inflation framed the new chair's task

stories.unplaced: A Senate vote; no event site.

stories.title: Trump–Xi Beijing summit: farm buys, Boeing jets, rare-earth access; H200 sales cleared
stories.summary: At a May 14–15 summit in Beijing, the White House said China committed to buy at least $17 billion a year of US farm goods through 2028 and 200 Boeing aircraft, and to improve rare-earth access. Reuters reported the US cleared Nvidia H200 sales to about 10 Chinese firms. Trump later said China had not bought the H200s.

causes.why: Losing IEEPA tariffs pushed Washington toward a negotiated truce
Chip controls are the main US bargaining chip

analysis.text: Beijing traded purchases for time and kept its real lever, rare-earth licensing, in place with a Nov 10 expiry. Refusing H200s signals it is betting on domestic chips.

stories.title: WHO declares the Congo–Uganda Ebola outbreak a global health emergency
stories.summary: The WHO declared an epidemic of Bundibugyo-virus Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The outbreak began in Congo's Ituri province, with cases in Kampala.

analysis.text: An epidemic in a war zone strains Kinshasa further and complicates any M23 settlement in the east.

stories.unplaced: Outbreak across Ituri and Uganda; no single site.

stories.title: China squeezes Japan over heavy rare earths
stories.summary: Reuters reported China cut off several heavy rare earths to Japan for at least four months, a repeat of its 2010 showdown. Japan's stockpiles, lower usage and other suppliers softened the blow.

causes.why: Coercion over Takaichi's Taiwan stance continued
State control of the sector makes targeted cut-offs possible

stories.title: UN warns of mass-atrocity risk as the RSF closes on El Obeid
stories.summary: The UN Security Council and the US State Department warned of the threat of atrocities by the RSF and allied forces around El Obeid, the North Kordofan capital sheltering large numbers of displaced people.

causes.why: Fighting shifted across Kordofan

stories.title: US and Iran sign the Islamabad Memorandum: blockade lifted, Hormuz reopened for 60 days
stories.summary: Trump and President Masoud Pezeshkian signed a memorandum ending military operations 'on all fronts, including in Lebanon'. The US lifted its blockade and issued oil waivers, and Iran agreed to free passage through Hormuz for 60 days while a final deal was negotiated. A separate US-brokered Israel–Lebanon 'Trilateral Framework' linked any Israeli pullback to verified disarmament of armed groups.

causes.why: Blockade pressure pushed both sides to a deal

stories.unplaced: The sources do not say where it was signed.

stories.title: Trump-endorsed outsider de la Espriella wins Colombia's presidency
stories.summary: Right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espriella narrowly beat leftist Iván Cepeda in Colombia's runoff, about 49.7% to 48.7% in the preliminary count. He has proposed handling relations with Venezuela through the US State Department.

causes.why: Ends the leftist turn that began with Petro's 2022 win

stories.unplaced: A national election; no single site.

stories.title: Starmer resigns after Reform UK's local-election surge
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigned after Labour lost about 1,500 council seats in the May 7 elections while Reform UK gained about 1,450. Andy Burnham succeeded him as prime minister on July 20.
stories.unplaced: A resignation announcement; no event site.
